reason: The text explicitly names Isaac (יִצְחָ֣ק), who is presented as a subordinate character following his father Abraham's will, not as a leader. While Abraham is clearly a leader (patriarch making decisions and giving commands), and God/Elohim could be considered a supreme authority figure, Isaac appears throughout the narrative in a passive, obedient role questioning his father and submitting to the test. The named characters include both Abraham (a leader) and Isaac (not a leader), contradicting the statement that only leaders are named.
